title: Metabolomics of ICH recovery (METABOL-ICH)
text:
Title: Metabolomics of Intracerebral Hemorrhage Outcomes (METABOL-ICHs)
Project Narrative:
Black American and Hispanic populations have roughly double the risk of brain hemorrhage, and
at a younger age, compared to populations of European descent. Brain hemorrhage is a toxic,
often deadly or highly disabling event, that leads to a wide variety of metabolic reactions and yet
to date, a comprehensive evaluation of these reactions has not been performed. We propose to
perform a comprehensive evaluation of the metabolic response from brain hemorrhage as well
as to identify those metabolic responses that associate with outcomes.

title: Closed-Loop Deep Brain Stimulation for Controlling Abnormal Neural Synchronization and Oscillations
text:
Neurophysiological and psychiatric disorders lead to severe cognitive impairments in patients and have been
attributed to pathological neural synchronization and abnormal oscillations in brain circuits associated with
specific diseases. The proposed computational study will facilitate the development of novel therapeutically
effective closed-loop deep-brain stimulation technologies for Parkinson’s disease and other neurophysiological
disorders caused by abnormal synchronous firing rhythms of neurons.

title: Leveraging machine learning and EMA data to identify factors that predict children's energy intake
text:
A better understanding of children’s eating behavior will lead to the development of innovative intervention
strategies for preventing childhood obesity. The current F32 application is designed to employ machine
learning techniques to identify factors that predict children’s eating behaviors based on ecological momentary
assessment (EMA) data. The findings of the proposed research have the potential to inform personalized
interventions that integrate EMA data and provide real-time feedback to promote healthy eating and prevent
childhood obesity.

title: Deciphering the hierarchical modularity of the mammalian cell through network integration and complex genetic perturbation strategies
text:
Genetic interactions govern the emergence of phenotype from genotype at every level, but our
capacity to probe and decipher these interactions is severely limited. We will continue our hybrid
computational and experimental effort to decipher the modular hierarchy of the mammalian cell,
how interactions govern the relationships between modules, and how rewiring these relationships
gives rise to disease states. Our development of next-generation multiplex CRISPR tools will
extend the current state of the art and enable researchers worldwide to gain deeper insight into
the complexity of the mammalian cell.

title: Animal Modeling Core
text: (Animal Modeling Core) The Animal Modeling Core (AMC) of the University of Michigan Skin Biology and Diseases Resource-based Center (UM-SBDRC) is a vital shared resource dedicated to the design, development, and characterization of mouse models to deepen our understanding of skin biology and disease. The AMC supports the overall mission of the UM-SBDRC and aligns with the NIAMS objective to facilitate impactful, translational research. Genetically-engineered mouse models (GEMMs) serve as indispensable tools for testing hypotheses generated by genomic and gene editing studies conducted in vitro or through the Functional Analytics Core (FAC). These in vivo models provide physiologically relevant insights into complex biological systems and disease mechanisms. Although many GEMMs are available through commercial vendors or repositories, project-specific models are frequently required. Unfortunately, many researchers face barriers due to the substantial time, cost, and expertise needed to develop and validate such models. Commercial services are often expensive and suboptimal. The AMC addresses these challenges by offering integrated, comprehensive GEMM development services and in vivo research support. Its continued long-term goal is to eliminate barriers for Center members and facilitate robust preclinical studies. During the current funding period, AMC-supported work has led to high-impact publications, new collaborations, and grant awards. Recognizing the unique contributions of in vivo studies—especially those involving multiple cell types within an intact organism—the AMC plays a critical role in advancing skin biology research from the bench to the clinic.

title: SCH: ASIC-Based Edge Al Wireless Vagus Nerve Implant for Exploring Diabetes Reversal.
text: This research explores a drug-free, implant-based Artificial Intelligence (AI) at-edge intervention for reversing Type 2 Diabetes (T2D), a condition affecting millions and driving significant healthcare costs. By targeting the vagus nerve, which connects the brain, stomach, and pancreas, this innovative intervention aims to restore the body’s natural ability to regulate blood sugar. The proposed implant can monitor and modulate neural activity in real time, potentially reducing or eliminating the need for medications or insulin. If successful, this intervention could provide a safer, more accessible, and minimally invasive solution for diabetes management, improving patient outcomes and reducing the overall burden of the disease.

title: Effects of early-life infection and immune signaling on neural development
text:
Infections in early childhood can cause long-term cognitive impairments, but the mechanisms by which
infection disrupts brain development are not well understood. This project uses a genetically tractable model
system to identify conserved immune and neurodevelopmental mechanisms linking early-life infection to
impaired brain growth and function.

title: Engineering Extracellular Vesicles for Tolerogenic Immunotherapy
text:
RESEARCH STRATEGY
Autoimmune diseases affect over 400 million people with increasing incidence. This proposal aims to develop
and test a new treatment for targeted treatment of autoimmune disease by harnessing immunosuppressive
extracellular vesicles as carriers for autoantigens to induce antigen-specific immune tolerance to treat
autoimmune disease. We will investigate how our technology suppresses T cell responses and will evaluate its
potential to treat autoimmune disease using a mouse model of multiple sclerosis.

title: Polygenic risk stratification combined with mpMRI to identify clinically relevant prostate cancer
text:
The premise of this proposal is that an optimal early detection strategy to identify clinically relevant prostate
cancer will involve a two-tiered algorithm that leverages inherited genetic information to determine who is at
risk for prostate cancer followed by MRI imaging to determine which of these high risk patients has clinically
relevant disease. We propose to test this premise by implementing a polygenic risk score in men and
conducting a prospective trial among 1,500 men with MRI to prove the two-tiered algorithm works.

title: Beyond blocking virus entry: Role of SERINC5 as a shield of genomic integrity
text:
The proposed research is relevant to public health because it will uncover how the cellular immune factor
SERINC5 protects from the attack of pathogens, including HIV-1, by selectively repressing their DNA. This
work will also reveal implications of this activity on the success of gene therapy delivery methods. The project
is relevant to NIH’s mission because the knowledge learned will provide the basis for the design of SERINC5-
based antivirals as well as tools to ensure successful delivery of therapeutic genes.

title: T32 Research Training in Academic Medical Oncology
text:
The University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center T32 Research Training in Academic Medical Oncology
Program is focused on training exceptionally talented and productive MDs and MD/PhDs for a research-
oriented career in academic medical oncology. These trainees are exposed to robust didactic, clinical, and lab-
based research training experiences as well as a broad range of structured career development opportunities
to position the T32 graduates to be the next generation of academically based leaders focused on novel
discoveries and clinical translation of their work to improve the lives and outcomes of patients with cancer.

title: Regulation of Candida albicans Pathogenesis by Protein Kinase and Transcription Factor Networks
text:
Candida albicans is the most common human fungal pathogen and affects both immunocompetent and
immunocompromised people. Understanding how C. albicans converts from a normal part of the microbiome to
a pathogen is important for identifying new ways to treat infections. Here, we propose to comprehensively
characterize genes that regulate the first two steps in the C. albicans pathogenic cycle using novel in vivo tools
and infection models.

title: Predictive Dosimetry and Metabolism Core
text:
The Predictive Dosimetry and Metabolism Core (PDMC) will provide OSU Superfund Research Center
investigators with tools and predictions of PAH dosimetry, enabling them to compare results across systems and
to translate experimental observations to real-world human exposures. The PDMC will rely on in silico tools to
predict PAH metabolites, chemical properties, mutagenicity, aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) binding, and
synergistic toxicity of PAH mixtures; to measure rates of PAH metabolism; to identify PAH metabolites via a
reference-free approach; and to predict PAH dosimetry in zebrafish, human lung cell culture systems, and human
populations.

title: Genomic Risk Variants in Orofacial Clefting: Discovery and Functional Validation
text:
The overall goal of this new collaborative project is to identify genomic risk variants for orofacial cleft (OFC)
birth defects in our large resource of OFC families and controls, and then to pursue the functional significance
of these variants in mouse models.

title: Microphysiological Systems to Study Hypoxic Cardiac Injury
text:
After a heart attack, there is a localized site of severe cardiac injury where the tissue experiences
poor blood perfusion, low oxygen levels, and death of the beating cells of the heart. Restoration
of blood flow is necessary but causes further damage to the heart, known as ischemia-reperfusion
injury. By engineering organ-on-a-chip microdevices to model these cardiac injuries, better
therapeutic strategies can be developed to minimize damage and promote repair.

title: Regulation of upstream open reading frames in mRNA stability and translation
text:
Upstream open reading frames (uORFs) are associated with numerous diseases, as they regulate mRNA
stability and translation. This study investigates uORF features and functions involved in mRNA decay and
translation controlled by evolutionarily conserved regulators using a model system that enables in vivo and
whole-organism level studies. Our findings could open doors to innovative diagnosis and treatment strategies.

title: A Drug Discovery Platform to Prioritize Development of Natural Product Neuromodulators for Treating Cognitive Impairment
text:
Mild Cognitive Impairment, associated with memory loss and changes in cognitive function, is one of the earliest
symptoms of Alzheimer’s Disease (MCI-AD). Botanical natural products (NPs) have shown to improve cognition
in AD patients, however incomplete descriptions of molecular targets, mechanisms, and appropriate brain
exposure have limited their development for MCI-AD. Sensorium Therapeutics is developing their Biodynamic
Discovery Platform (BDP) to identify and develop psychoactive natural products to treat AD by delaying MCI
onset after the earliest signals of pathology can be detected.

title: Mechanisms of uterine artery hemodynamics adaptation to pregnancy and gestational hypoxia
text:
Program Narrative
Pregnancy is associated with a striking increase of uterine blood flow that is essential for normal fetal
development as well as for cardiovascular well-being of the mother. Hypoxia during pregnancy has profound
adverse effects on uterine artery hemodynamics adaptation, increasing incidence of pregnancy complications of
preeclampsia and fetal intrauterine growth restriction. Yet, much remains unknown of the mechanisms
underlying maternal cardiovascular adaptation to chronic hypoxia during pregnancy. Scientifically, the proposed
study will augment our understanding of basic mechanisms whereby maternal cardiovascular system adapts to
pregnancy and gestational hypoxia. From a clinical standpoint, the study will provide new insights and suggest
new directions in the management of pregnancy complications and abnormal fetal development associated with
gestational hypoxia, thereby reducing perinatal morbidity and mortality while improving maternal health and
neonatal outcome.

title: Engineering ferritin degrader-encapsulated platelets for post-surgical TNBC treatment
text:
Post-surgical TNBC recurrence is the major cause of the poor prognosis of TNBC patients. This proposal aims
to identify intracellular ferritin as a new TNBC therapeutic target and develop a ferritin-degrading proteolysis
targeting chimeras (PROTACs) molecule to leverage the intracellular ubiquitin-proteasome system to degrade
ferritin to induce the TNBC cell pyroptosis. The endogenous platelets will be applied to encapsulate developed
ferritin degraders for enhanced in vivo pharmacokinetics and anti-TNBC recurrence efficacy, which can serve as
monotherapy or synergize with current immunotherapeutics to prevent post-surgical TNBC recurrence.

title: A Modular Overground Balance Walkway for Task-Specific Perturbation-based Fall Prevention Assessment and Training
text:
Falls are a major public health concern for older adults, resulting in significant injuries, disabilities, and fatalities
each year, as well as over $50 billion in annual healthcare costs in the U.S. This project will develop and test
the MOdular BALance (MOBAL) Perturbation Walkway, a clinic-ready system that provides safe, realistic
balance challenges to assess and train the sensorimotor, cognitive, and psychological factors contributing to
fall risk. Successful implementation will enable more effective fall prevention and rehabilitation for high-risk
populations, improving quality of life and reducing costly, preventable injuries nationwide.
